function.name: get_url_content

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

Below is a quick‑reference guide to the main “tools” people typically rely on when looking to book air travel—whether through a website/app, via an API integration, or even manually at an airport kiosk. (If you’re building your own system, see the **API** section for programmatic options.) | Category | Tool / Service | Typical Use Case | |----------|-----------------|------------------| | **Online Aggregator Sites & Apps** | • Google Flights
• Skyscanner
• Kayak
• Momondo
• Expedia
• Priceline
• Orbitz
• Travelocity | Search across many carriers, compare prices, filter by layovers/duration, read reviews. Most offer both desktop and mobile experiences. | | **Airline Direct Booking Platforms** | • American Airlines – AA.com
• Delta Air Lines – Delta.com
• United Airlines – United.com
• Southwest – Southwest.com
• British Airways – BA.com
• Lufthansa – Lufthansa.com
…and hundreds more worldwide | Book directly with the carrier, often getting better seat selection, loyalty points, and easier changes/cancellations. | | **Mobile Flight‑Booking Apps** | • TripIt (itinerary organizer)
• Hopper (price prediction + alerts)
• FlightRadar24 (flight tracking)
• SITA Mobile (for frequent flyers)
• Airbnb Experiences (occasionally includes local tours after flight). | Manage itineraries on-the-go, receive push notifications for gate changes, delays, price drops. | | **Corporate & Group Booking Systems** | • Concur Travel & Expense
• SAP Ariba Travel
• Egencia (by Expedia)
• Amex Corporate Travel Services | Handle bulk bookings, enforce corporate policies, integrate expense reporting. | | **Airport Kiosk & Self‑Service Terminals** | • Self‑check‑in kiosks (most airports)
• Baggage drop‑off machines | Quick check‑ins, printing boarding passes, rebooking missed connections. | | **Programmatic APIs (for developers)** | • Amadeus for Developers – Global distribution system (GDS) API.
• Sabre Dev Studio – GDS API suite.
• Travelport Universal API.
• SkyScanner Rapid API.
• Kiwi.com API.
• OpenSky Network API (real‑time flight status).
• Google Flights Data API (limited public access). | Build custom booking engines, retrieve fare quotes, manage reservations, fetch real‑time flight status. | ### How These Tools Fit Together 1. **Search & Compare:** Start with an aggregator (e.g., Skyscanner or Google Flights) to find the best route/time/price combo. 2. **Book Directly if Needed:** Once you’ve found a suitable option, you might prefer to book straight with the airline’s site to lock in mileage accruals or special fares. 3. **Manage Your Trip:** After booking, use a mobile app (like Hopper or the airline’s official app) to keep track of gates, delays, and itinerary updates. 4. **For Businesses:** Leverage corporate systems (Concur, SAP Ariba) to automate approvals, capture expenses, and maintain compliance. --- #### Quick Tips * **Price Alerts:** Many aggregators let you set alerts so you’ll be notified when fares dip. * **Flexible Dates:** Look for flexible‑date searches—they often reveal cheaper alternatives just a day earlier/later. * **Hidden Fees:** Check baggage fees separately; low‑fare tickets sometimes come with high extra charges. * **Frequent Flyer Status:** When possible, book through the airline’s portal to earn miles or elite benefits. Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any particular platform, how to integrate one into a workflow, or recommendations tailored to a specific region or budget!
